clue.text: Barney runs pub in centre

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: in says the word for pub sits inside the word for centre

parts.note: a hub is the centre of activity
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A rowdy argument breaks out at the pub in the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: Barney is British slang for a noisy row, and so is rhubarb, also the murmur actors make to sound like a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British colloquialisms for a noisy quarrel or meaningless chatter.

clue.text: Spiritual leader with little time for talk

parts.note: a rabbi leads a Jewish congregation
T is a short abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A religious leader with a few minutes for conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit on is British slang for chatter, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal speech, to rabbit is to chatter at length.

clue.text: Result from university professor's first attempt

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of professor's is used

parts.note: a shot is an attempt

explanation.surface: The outcome of an academic's first try.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the final outcome or consequence of something.

clue.text: A Conservative politician supporting company line is hard to reach

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes below, so the politician follows the company

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A Tory politician backing the company line is hard to get hold of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' places MP under CO in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a goal is to achieve or attain it.

clue.text: Graduate caught working for artist

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A graduate is caught working on behalf of a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was a celebrated twentieth-century Irish-born British painter.

clue.text: Desperate doctor has to leave hospital with nervous twitch

indicators.note: to leave says the hospital letter departs from the word has

parts.note: taken as written
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A frantic doctor must quit the hospital because of an uncontrollable twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes H out of HAS, leaving AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate measures are extreme ones, which is what drastic means.

clue.text: Loud noise, then resent broken crockery

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

indicators.note: broken suggests the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A crash, then annoyance at the smashed plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges RESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A matched collection of plates and dishes for dinner is a set of crockery.

clue.text: Reason Republican's dismissed fever

indicators.note: dismissed says the Republican letter is sent away from the word

parts.note: to reason with someone is to argue
R is the abbreviation for Republican; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A cause given for why a Republican was sacked: illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is an old word for a malarial fever with shivering.

clue.text: Pilot won't welcome this dog on journey

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or tail them
a spin is a short drive or trip

explanation.surface: An airman would not be glad to see this dog on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like a noun but is the verb to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane spiralling nose-down out of control is a dreaded event for any aviator.

clue.text: Meet prisoner on border

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
a verge is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Visit an inmate at the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that converge come together at a point.

clue.text: Key turned in panic is abandoned

indicators.note: turned says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A key is turned while panic sets in and the place is abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word; it is the signal that the letters lie within the next words.
explanation.definitionFit: Key as an adjective means fundamental or essential, a near synonym.

clue.text: Army leader from Turin, once, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of the two words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A general who came from Turin in the old days, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TURIN and ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman officer commanding a hundred soldiers was a leader within the army.

clue.text: Shopkeeper renting room, shivering when temperature drops

indicators.note: shivering suggests the letters are shaken into a new order
drops says the temperature letter falls out of the word renting

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper letting out a room shivers as the temperature falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes T from RENTING to give RENING; 'shivering' rearranges RENING with ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardware dealer selling tools and household goods is a kind of shopkeeper.

clue.text: Man, maybe, is allowed no conclusion

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: no conclusion says the word for allowed loses its final letter

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: A man, perhaps, is permitted no ending to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man; the capital is hidden at the start of the clue. 'no conclusion' trims LET to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man in the Irish Sea is an example of an island.

clue.text: Gang in America can pick up socialist papers secured here?

parts.note: a ring is a criminal gang
an American trash can is a bin elsewhere

indicators.note: pick up in a down clue says the word is read upwards

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist

explanation.surface: Can an American gang pick up left-wing papers here?
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick up' turns RED to DER in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A folder with metal hoops holds punched sheets in place.

clue.text: Simple aircraft's weak by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the words are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: an aircraft is a plane, and weak is ailing: plane's ailing

explanation.surface: A basic aeroplane is feeble, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a task that proceeds smoothly and easily, so it is simple.

clue.text: Annoyed at dirtier bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Fed up with bananas going grubbier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges AT DIRTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritated and annoyed are synonyms for vexed.

clue.text: Rising editor stopped dead

indicators.note: Rising in a down clue says the letters read upwards

parts.note: ceased means stopped

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming editor stopped dead in their tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns ED to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: The deceased are people who have died.

clue.text: Prevent Democrat changing US ideas

indicators.note: changing suggests the letters are altered into another order

explanation.surface: Stop a Democrat altering American thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges US IDEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk someone out of acting is to stop or deter them.

clue.text: Plan for leaving tyre gets taxi damaged

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: A tyre gets a taxi damaged, so a way out is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges TYRE GETS TAXI.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a planned way to withdraw from a situation or venture.

clue.text: In a hotel, enthralled by scholarly book

indicators.note: enthralled by says the hotel letter is held inside the book

parts.note: a tome is a large weighty book
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Inside a hotel, captivated by a learned volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in is to be present at one's residence rather than out.

clue.text: Pressing uniform finally for chap

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: finally says only the last letter of the word for is used

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman or chap

explanation.surface: Ironing a uniform at last for a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' looks like ironing beside uniform but means demanding attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing matter is one needing immediate attention.

clue.text: Vegan, say, oddly rejected piece of cake

indicators.note: oddly rejected says the letters in odd positions are thrown out, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A vegan, for example, turned down a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: From VEGANSAY drop V, G, N, A to keep E, A, S, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an idiom for something effortless.

clue.text: Relative rung by nurse

parts.note: a rung of a ladder is a step
in Britain a sister is a senior nurse

explanation.surface: A relative was telephoned by a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rung' looks like the past of ring as in telephone, but is the noun, a ladder's step.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter of one's step-parent is a family member by marriage.

clue.text: Satisfaction from parking vehicle

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a ride is informal for a car or vehicle

explanation.surface: Pleasure gained from parking one's car.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride is the sense of satisfaction in one's own achievement.

clue.text: Perfect husband embraces like that

indicators.note: embraces says the letters sit held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An ideal spouse hugs in exactly that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus means in this way, or like that.

clue.text: Type of western food

definitions.meaning: a cowboy film made cheaply in Italy, in the manner of Sergio Leone
long thin pasta strands are a food

explanation.surface: A sort of Western cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian-made cowboy films earned a pasta nickname, and the pasta itself is a staple food.

clue.text: Finished trapping queen bee

indicators.note: trapping says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: done means finished
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A queen bee is caught and finished off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen bee' reads as one phrase, but queen gives R and bee alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A male honeybee that does no work is called this.

clue.text: Turned out daughter brought back most of pudding

indicators.note: brought back says the shortened word is read backwards
most of says the word for pudding loses its last letter

parts.note: pudding is the British word for dessert

explanation.surface: A daughter returned with nearly all of the pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims DESSERT to DESSER; 'brought back' turns it to RESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Well turned out means smartly clothed, so the phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Serious tear in vest when tops are removed

indicators.note: when tops are removed says each of the three words loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A grave rip appears in a vest once its upper parts are taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing T, I and V from TEAR IN VEST leaves EAR, N, EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest and serious are synonyms for sincere and grave in manner.
